key_insight: Bubble curtains in lock-exchange flows exhibit three distinct subregimes within the breakthrough regime, and their behavior depends on both air Froude number and the salt-to-freshwater density ratio.
engineering_relevance: This means bubble-curtain design for ship locks must account for fluid-property ratios, not just curtain strength, to better block salt transport and improve operational performance.
method: Two-phase large-eddy simulations of a laboratory-scale lock-exchange setup
Detailed analysis of flow and density fields around a bubble curtain
Comparison across conditions to identify distinct flow subregimes and transport effects
evidence_signal: The study uses simulation-based hydrodynamic and density-field analysis to show regime classification and salt-transport blocking effectiveness vary with air Froude number and density ratio.
watch_item: Results are from laboratory-scale simulations, so full-scale lock performance may differ and should be validated before design changes.
paper_title: Lock-exchange flow regimes under low air Froude number bubble curtains
